newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank meets, no interest rate change expected.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank meets, no interest rate change expected.

text.p: The policy-making council of Germany's Bundesbank began its regular meeting on Thursday with financial markets confident that this week there would be no surprise policy changes from the central bank.
Two weeks ago, the Bundesbank shocked markets with a larger than expected cut in its main money market rate, the securities repurchase rate or repo, to three percent from 3.30 percent.
Its discount and Lombard rates -- the floor and ceiling for German money market rates -- were held unchanged at 2.50 percent and 4.50 percent respectively, in line with expectations.

Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer made clear in a statement soon after the rate cut announcement that markets should not expect any further policy moves for some time and a Reuter poll of economists this week showed this message had been taken to heart.

All 10 of the economists polled said they did not expect any change in policy and predicted that the Bundesbank would set another two securities repurchase tenders at an unchanged rate of three percent.

Other possibilities open to the central bank would be to refrain from announcing its upcoming money market tenders for the next two weeks after today's meeting -- delaying any announcement until next Tuesday when the tender is set.
The central bank could also theoretically switch to a variable rate securities repurchase tender. But markets and analysts believe this is a very unlikely option.
